original_star_baseline.notes: Current phase6 speedup calculations use these baseline numbers.

implemented_code_paths: STAR transformer now always uses SGLang LocalAttention on the single-GPU path, so requested attention backends such as FlashAttention are actually honored.
STAR transformer already exposes SGLang backend capability metadata for FA/SAGE and distributed USPAttention on parallel paths.
STAR cache-dit adapter registration exists in runtime/models/dits/star_cogvideox_sr.py.
STAR Nunchaku/SVDQuant quantization rules exist in runtime/models/dits/star_cogvideox_sr.py.
GPU worker now clears CUDA allocator cache between requests when torch.compile is enabled, which stabilized STAR repeated-request compile benchmarking.

STAR transformer input/post/final layernorm plus modulation paths now use SGLang-compatible fused layernorm-scale-shift and residual-layernorm-scale-shift helpers while preserving STAR state_dict names.
STAR qk layernorm now uses a compile-safe compatibility path: contiguous CUDA tensors still route to SGLang LayerNorm, while non-CUDA paths fall back to fp32 layer_norm for correctness.
STAR local enhancer has a 5D-compatible experimental implementation, but benchmark evidence shows it should remain disabled on the single-card exact path.

STAR condition-video VAE encoding can now proactively release text-encoder GPU residency and, when explicitly requested, temporarily offload the transformer before VAE encode to avoid compile warmup-to-measured OOMs.
STAR includes an optional FlashInfer RoPE path, but phase7 benchmark evidence shows it should remain disabled for the mainline STAR exact configuration.
STAR single-GPU quantization now threads quant_config through time_embed, qkv/out, MLP, AdaLN, final layer, and text projection, so ReplicatedLinear hot paths can really use FP8/AWQ/SVDQuant hooks.
STAR manual smoke/profile/matrix scripts now expose phase7 controls for FlashInfer RoPE, local enhancer mode, resident strategy, and text-encoder release policy.

STAR sampling defaults and manual acceptance scripts now resolve STAR output playback to 8 FPS by default, or inherit the reference/condition clip FPS when available, which fixes the accelerated 1-second single-card mp4 artifacts.
TextEncodingStage now reloads text encoders automatically on the next request after VAE-stage peak-memory eviction, fixing the resident fast-path device mismatch on repeated requests.

STAR ModelOpt FP8 loading now accepts squeezed singleton block scales and auto-dequantizes BF16 fallback modules from weight_scale_inv tensors, which makes the STAR FP8 checkpoint load and pass baseline parity.
Manual benchmark/profile scripts exist for STAR phase6/7 profiling and matrix experiments.
current_gaps: Single-card exact path has not reached the target 1.6x/1.8x speedup band.

The current HEAD can keep compile warmup-to-measured exact generation stable only when temporary transformer offload is enabled before condition-video VAE encode, and that still leaves single-card exact well below the target band.
The repaired STAR FP8 checkpoint now passes baseline parity and slightly beats the best exact result, but it still tops out at about 1.4322x warm speedup and fails the stricter parity profile.
Batched CFG did not produce a meaningful single-card gain on this STAR workload.
The phase7 fused layernorm/modulation path improved single-card compile speed slightly, but the gain is still far from the final phase7 target band.
FlashInfer RoPE was integrated and benchmarked, but it regressed STAR single-card exact speed and should remain disabled.
Keeping the text encoder resident between requests still OOMs during condition-video VAE encoding, even when the transformer is quantized to FP8.
The current FP8 + TeaCache + cache-dit probe showed no measurable per-step gain over plain FP8 compile on this STAR workload.

Historical single-card benchmark videos produced before the STAR FPS fix were written at 24 FPS instead of the reference 8 FPS, so those older mp4 artifacts should not be used for subjective playback comparison.
SAGE, SAGE_ATTN_3, and AITER cannot be recommended in the current environment because sageattention and aiter are not installed on this L20 host.
Nunchaku SVDQuant is not currently usable in this environment because the nunchaku package is absent and L20 (SM89) is outside the supported architecture set.

runs.label: dual_cfg_parallel
notes: Current best quality-passing speedup result.
This already exceeds the 1.8x warm speedup threshold, but it is a 2-GPU result.

runs.label: single_fa_old_probe
notes: Historical single-card FA probe before the latest explicit single-GPU LocalAttention fix.

runs.label: single_fa_exact
notes: This run verified that single-GPU STAR now really uses SGLang FlashAttention.
Quality stayed aligned, but speedup remained far below the single-card target band.

runs.label: single_fa_batched_cfg
notes: Batched CFG produced no meaningful single-card speedup on this STAR workload.
This path is currently lower priority than quantization and cache work.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_warm_v1
notes: First compile benchmark attempt.
The warmup request succeeded and was already much faster than the exact non-compile path.
The second request OOMed before VAE encode, which motivated the worker-side empty_cache stabilization change.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_warm_v2
notes: Current best exact single-card result.
Quality still passes baseline parity and improved slightly over the non-compile exact path.
Single-card exact speedup is now meaningfully better, but still below the 1.6x / 1.8x phase6 target band.

runs.label: single_compile_cache_combo_v2
notes: Current best single-card exact result, but only marginally better than pure compile.
TeaCache plus cache-dit did not unlock an additional step-function speedup under the current parameter set.

runs.label: single_teacache_cache_compile_probe
notes: This probe did not show a compelling gain.
It was measured without compile warmup averaging, so it is not the final word on torch.compile.

runs.label: single_fp8_probe
notes: FP8 is the most promising single-card speed path tested so far, but parity is badly broken.
This is now one of the highest-priority remaining phase6 gaps.

runs.label: single_fa_no_offload
notes: OOM during condition-video VAE encode after loading both text encoder and transformer on GPU.

runs.label: single_fa_transformer_on_gpu
notes: Keeping the transformer resident on GPU still OOMs before denoising begins, so exact single-card speedups are memory-bound.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_fusedln_v1
notes: First phase7 fused layernorm attempt.
torch.compile failed in qk layernorm because LayerNorm.forward_cuda used view() on a non-contiguous query/key tensor.
This failure led to the compile-safe qk layernorm compatibility fix used by v2.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_fusedln_v2
notes: This is the current best exact single-card result.
Compared with single_fa_compile_warm_v2, the phase7 fused layernorm/modulation path improved warm_e2e_speedup from 1.4153x to 1.4314x.
The gain is real but still far from the final single-card phase7 target band.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_fusedln_local5d_v1
notes: The 5D local-enhancer rewrite was numerically correct and passed baseline parity.
It regressed exact single-card speed relative to single_fa_compile_fusedln_v2, so it should remain disabled on the mainline STAR path.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_ropefused_v1
notes: First FlashInfer RoPE integration attempt.
Failed because the synthesized RoPE cache had been registered as a new persistent buffer, which the FSDP loader correctly rejected as an unsupported checkpoint-state addition.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_ropefused_v2
notes: Second FlashInfer RoPE integration attempt.
Compilation failed because the first runtime-cache implementation produced a meta tensor inside the compiled graph when the model had been initialized from a meta-device state.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_ropefused_v3
notes: FlashInfer RoPE warmup request completed successfully.
The measured request OOMed during condition-video VAE encode because the compiled transformer residency increased peak memory before denoising began.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_ropefused_v4
notes: This was the first fully stable FlashInfer-RoPE exact run after adding the pre-encode transformer offload guard.
It passed baseline parity but materially regressed exact single-card speed, so FlashInfer RoPE should remain disabled for STAR.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_stable_v5
notes: This is the current stable single-card exact configuration on HEAD.
Disabling FlashInfer RoPE helped, but compile warmup-to-measured stability still requires the pre-encode transformer offload guard, and that cost drags speed down to about 1.27x.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_mainline_v6
notes: This run used the current mainline transformer path with FlashInfer RoPE disabled and without the pre-encode transformer offload guard.
The warmup request succeeded, but the measured request still OOMed during condition-video VAE encode, so the mainline compile path is not yet stable across requests.

runs.label: single_fa_compile_keeptext_transformer_guard_v1
notes: After fixing the resident fast-path text-encoder reload bug, the exact keep-text variant still OOMed during condition-video VAE encode on the first request.
This confirms that STAR cannot keep the text encoder resident between requests on a single L20 while also preserving the no-global-offload exact path.

runs.label: single_fp8_compile_keeptext_transformer_guard_v1
notes: Even with the STAR FP8 transformer, keeping the text encoder resident between requests still OOMed during condition-video VAE encode.
The quantized transformer reduces denoise cost, but it does not free enough memory to support a text-encoder-resident single-card path on this host.

runs.label: single_fp8_full_v1
notes: This run uses the repaired STAR FP8 loading path: singleton block scales now load correctly, and BF16 fallback modules such as temp_local.conv1 are auto-dequantized from weight_scale_inv tensors.
Baseline parity passed and the result is marginally faster than the best exact single-card run, so phase7 now has a baseline-passing quantized STAR configuration.
Strict parity still fails and the speedup remains far below the 1.6x/1.8x single-card phase7 target band.
This artifact was written before the STAR FPS fix and saves the 25-frame output at 24 FPS, so it should not be used for subjective playback comparison against the original 8 FPS STAR video.

runs.label: single_fp8_full_v2_fps_fix
notes: This rerun verifies the STAR FPS fix: the candidate mp4 is now written at 8 FPS, matching the 25-frame, ~3.1-second playback semantics of the original STAR reference video.
Baseline parity passed again and visual metrics improved over single_fp8_full_v1, but strict parity still fails.
Warm speedup measured 1.3919x on this rerun, so the single-card phase7 target band is still not met.
